newsitem.title: USA: New Mexico tries again on electric restructuring.
newsitem.headline: New Mexico tries again on electric restructuring.

text.p: The New Mexico Public Utility Commission on Tuesday postponed a new rate case for the Public Service Company of New Mexico, while ordering the utility and other parties involved in the debate over electric industry restructuring to resume negotiations.
The talks are expected to reopen next week.
The collaborative talks had stalled two weeks ago when consumer groups and PNM were unable to reach agreement on key issues such as who should control power generation.
The commission also revised its rules to expedite the negotiations and postoned PNM's next rate case to October 1.
Depending on the outcome of the restructuring talks, the commission will determine at a later date whether the rate case is necessary.
The collaborative talks will continue until September 15.
When the process is complete, the commission said it would report the results to the legislative interim committee charged with studying industry restructuring.
"We're pleased the commission has reaffirmed its support of a collaborative approach to industry restructuring," said PNM chief executive officer Ben Montoya.
